item.title: How a record El Niño is hitting your wallet
item.description:
Today we're bringing you an episode from our friends at Short Wave on the economic toll this year's El Niño could have. 

Peru's anchovy industry, the largest single-species fishery in the world, is being rocked by the ongoing El Niño . It's not the first time the fishery has been impacted by the natural weather phenomenon — El Niño gets its name from Peruvian fishermen. And it's a stark reminder of the reverberating economic consequences of El Niño events, which can cost the global economy trillions of dollars.

item.description:

item.title: Why the 'good old days' of American manufacturing are long gone
item.description:
Harvard professor Willy Shih tells us why the manufacturing renaissance President Trump envisioned has not come to pass and how a different type of resurgence may still be possible. 

Willy Shih’s book is Where Does My Stuff Come From?: The Powerful Economics Behind Global Supply Chains.

Fact checking by Sierra Juarez.
